narrative.overview: Prism NR is drawn the way Ryoji Ikeda draws data: pure black, pure white, hairline bars and dense tabular numerals. Every barcode on screen is real information. Colour exists only as spectral dispersion, as 2px strokes. Selection is inversion. Motion is maximal by the user's decision, with large-area flashes held at or below three per second.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground, white ink, two greys for hierarchy, no other neutrals.
One monospace face for all Latin text and numerals; Chinese falls back to Microsoft YaHei UI.
Square corners everywhere; hairline rules carry all structure.
Barcodes and bar lattices are data encodings, each legible as a measurement.
Selection by inversion with a clip-path wipe.

rules.name: The Dispersion Rule
rules.body: Spectral colours appear only as 2px bars, strokes or barcode segments that carry a state. A spectral fill behind text is never used.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The only filled highlight is white. Anything selected, current or primary becomes white with black ink.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number uses tabular figures so values align across rows and roll in place without jitter.

dos: Do encode real data in every barcode or bar run; label estimates as 估算.
Do use inversion (#ffffff field, #000000 ink) for every selected or primary state.
Do keep spectral colours to 2px state marks.
Do keep large-area flashes at or below three per second at every motion level.
donts: Don't add rounded corners, shadows, gradients or glass.
Don't introduce greys beyond #8c8c8c and #5c5c5c, or tint the black.
Don't draw barcodes or bars that encode nothing.
Don't use NVIDIA green or RGB gamer styling.
